name: Remorse-Frost
geological_features: Methane ice plains extending pole to pole
Cryovolcanoes erupting slurries of ammonia and water ice
Wind-sculpted ice formations called penitentes covering vast areas
specific_features: An abandoned research station with all personnel missing and no sign of evacuation
description: Remorse-Frost is a desolate ice world where methane ice plains stretch from pole to pole in an unbroken sheet of frozen regret. Cryovolcanoes dot the surface, erupting slurries of ammonia and water ice that freeze into grotesque formations within seconds of exposure to the atmosphere. Fields of penitentes, blade-like ice formations sculpted by sublimation, cover the equatorial regions in forests of frozen razors.

The thin atmosphere barely qualifies as such, a wisp of nitrogen and methane that does nothing to moderate the killing cold. The silence here has a quality of finality to it, as though sound itself has given up on this world and retreated to warmer places.

An automated research station was established on the surface twelve years ago to study cryovolcanic activity, staffed by a rotating crew of six scientists. During a routine communication check, the station went silent. The rescue team found the facility intact and fully powered, personal effects undisturbed, meals half-eaten on the table, but all six personnel were gone without any record of departure.

No bodies were found. No distress signal was sent. The station's external cameras recorded nothing but the endless ice. Subsequent investigations found no evidence of foul play, environmental failure, or psychological break, only absence. Remorse-Frost has been classified as a restricted zone pending resolution of the disappearances, but the case remains open and cold as the world itself.
